findings.reason: the section must state that every new call site passes the inventoried checkout (`docs_dir`), and must not adopt `declared_for`'s `None` as the precedent, or it re-introduces the cross-tree read it exists to remove.
findings.text: §15 holds `declared_for` up as the pattern for reaching file-aware section identity ("the file-aware declarations the roadmap already resolves (`_plan_declarations`, roadmap.py:128, as declared_for does)"), but `declared_for` calls `_plan_declarations(target, None, project, target_slug)` and a `None` `docs_dir` makes that reader fall back to `_load_mounts()` — the registered mount, not the checkout the rows were inventoried from — which is exactly the cross-tree defect §7's review already repaired once, so a worktree-scoped roadmap would judge one tree's refs against another tree's declarations; the sites §15 moves (reckon/roadmap.py:831 `_after_edges`, 947 `_section_scoped_edges`) receive neither `docs_dir` today and would collide with the same fallback.

findings.reason: the node must be told once whether reckon/crew/promotion.py:7273 keeps the narrow `plan_section_anchors` (missing a typed-record-only section) or moves to `declared_section_identities`, because the two readings put different sections in the unlanded pickup list.
findings.text: §15 says `plan_section_anchors` "keeps its narrower meaning … for callers that want only those: promotion.py:7273 lists unlanded anchors", then three sentences later lists the same site as one of the callers that must move because it "enumerates a plan's sections … so it reaches the owner too"; `_plan_remaining_sections` (reckon/crew/promotion.py:7251) does ask the existence question, since it is the fallback that enumerates section identities when `section_declarations` is not a mapping, so the two instructions cannot both be implemented as written.
